title: The Jamāʿa of 1379 takes up the question of the capital. The expansion north has left Gharnāṭa isolated, a long ride from the frontier, and the court finds itself cut off from its slowly integrating lands. The old idea of a capital at Qurṭuba is raised again, and then a second proposal: invest in the sea, set the Catalan shipwrights, now the Emperor's subjects, to building a trading fleet, and move the capital to Ishbīliya, where its power would reach furthest

proposals.Qurṭuba: the old idea: the caliphs' capital, at the centre of al-Andalus
proposals.Ishbīliya: a capital on the river and the sea, with a trading fleet built by the Catalan shipwrights

data.why: Gharnāṭa is far from the northern frontier and from the new lands; the court is decentralised from them
